role: The join packet: entity id, gametype, hardcore, dimension, difficulty, max players and world type. It is what puts the client into the play state.

members.name: field_149206_a (entity id)
members.note: the player's entity id comes from the snapshot's entity record, not the packet

members.name: field_149205_c (gametype)
members.note: survival is implicit; the native client has no gametype state; not a gap (triage 2026-09-25)

members.name: field_149202_d (dimension)
members.note: the snapshot records the dimension the player is in

members.name: field_149203_e (difficulty)
members.note: surv_world_setup takes the difficulty from the run's conf/snapshot

members.name: S01PacketJoinGame
members.note: never constructed natively: the client world initializes from the snapshot instead; not a gap (triage 2026-09-25)

members.name: readPacketData
members.note: wire framing; the native engine has no network

members.name: processPacket
members.note: handleJoinGame's observable work (client world init, spawn position, difficulty) is what the snapshot load and serverreplay's join replay (chunkload.c:cl_login at serverreplay.c:892) reproduce

members.name: serialize
members.note: Packet.serialize is logging only: MessageSerializer's and MessageDeserializer's debug lines, which the local channel does not have

notes: The join's chunk streaming (the login queue, radius 10 spiral order, the tick-1 view distance change) is replayed at the server side: serverreplay.c around line 866 and cl_login (chunkload.c:1348). Not gaps (triage 2026-09-25, out/plan/remaining-2026-09-25.md): the join is the snapshot load. Formerly listed as missing: No native counterpart builds or processes the packet itself; every field's effect arrives through the snapshot manifest and the serverreplay join (PlayerManager.addPlayer with the parked position, then the view-distance change).
